about: Domaine Eden is the second estate of Mount Eden Vineyards, one of California’s most storied mountain wineries. Martin Ray planted Mount Eden’s vineyards on a 2,000-foot peak above Saratoga in 1945, and Jeffrey and Ellie Patterson have run the estate since 1981 (Jeffrey as winemaker). In 2007 Mount Eden bought the neighbouring Cinnabar winery and vineyard, one ridge to the south, which engineer Tom Mudd founded in 1983 and first planted in the mid-1980s. Renamed Domaine Eden, it sits about a mile from Mount Eden as the crow flies.

Domaine Eden’s soils differ from the Franciscan shale at Mount Eden, and the importer says the wines show more open varietal fruit and a broader mid-palate than the stony estate bottlings. The Cabernet is a true Bordeaux blend: in 2019, 81% Cabernet Sauvignon with 14% Merlot and small amounts of Cabernet Franc, Petit Verdot and Malbec. The vineyards are dry-farmed and fermentations rely on native yeasts, the hands-off approach Patterson uses at Mount Eden.

Critics praised the 2019. Antonio Galloni of Vinous called it plush, deep and seductive, with black plum and tobacco, and Wine Enthusiast’s Matt Kettmann noted fresh lines of blackberry. Expect loamy earth, currant, blackberry and cedar on the nose, bright blue fruit on the palate and well-knit tannins. It is drinking well now and should keep until about 2035.
facts: 81% Cabernet Sauvignon, 14% Merlot, 2% Cabernet Franc, 2% Petit Verdot, 1% Malbec
Domaine Eden (former Cinnabar estate), planted mid-1980s
